title: A field-uniform Picard exponent for a connected affine algebraic group
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be a smooth connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There exists an integer $n\geq1$ such that, for every field extension $K/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] and every invertible $\mathcal O_{G_K}$-module $N$ [def-sc-invertible-module], one has $N^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal O_{G_K}$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Here $G_K=G\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ is the scheme fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. The same integer $n$ works for all extensions, including transcendental and inseparable extensions, and all such $N$. The trivial group is allowed. Equivalently, the groups of isomorphism classes of invertible modules on $G_K$, with tensor product as addition, are all annihilated by $n$.

source.place: WANTED locally: M. Brion, On Linearization of Line Bundles, J. Math. Sci. Univ. Tokyo 22 (2015), pp.113–147, Lemma 2.3 and Proposition 2.5, printed pp.117–119. Primary publisher PDF read online. Specialization to algebraically closed k; no group action on a second scheme is involved. Milne, Algebraic Groups (2017), Corollary 18.23, p.393, supplies the finite Picard group over k but does not alone supply the field-uniform assertion.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-picard-trivial-multiplicative-cover], choose a smooth connected affine group $P$ and a multiplicative isogeny $f:P\to G$ with $\operatorname{Pic}(P)=0$. Its scheme-theoretic kernel $A$ is $D(M)=\operatorname{Spec}k[M]$ for a finite abelian group $M$, with the Hopf algebra described in that node. All these choices are over $k$ and precede any choice of $K$.

source.place: Proposition 18.22 and Corollary 18.23, printed pp.392–393; Proposition 18.18, sequence (129), printed p.391.

proof.text: Choose a positive integer annihilating $M$ explicitly. Put $q=|M|$. For each $m\in M$, two of $0,m,\ldots,qm$ coincide, so some $1\le r_m\le q$ satisfies $r_m m=0$. Set $n=\prod_{m\in M}r_m\ge1$; then $nm=0$ for every $m$. In the Hopf algebra of $A=D(M)$ from [lem-sfb-picard-trivial-multiplicative-cover], multiplication by $n$ pulls $e^m$ back to $e^{nm}=1$. Thus $[n]_A$ is the trivial homomorphism as a scheme morphism, including when $A$ is nonreduced. For every character $\chi:A\to\mathbf G_m$, its pointwise $n$th power equals $\chi\circ[n]_A$, hence is trivial. Consequently $nX^*(A)=0$.

source.place: Proposition 18.22 and Corollary 18.23, printed pp.392–393; Proposition 18.18, sequence (129), printed p.391.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-character-picard-isogeny-sequence] to $f:P\to G$. Its hypotheses hold by step 1, including the finite diagonalizable scheme-theoretic kernel. Exactness gives $X^*(A)\xrightarrow{\delta}\operatorname{Pic}(G)\xrightarrow{f^*}\operatorname{Pic}(P)=0$. Hence $\delta$ is surjective. For any $a\in\operatorname{Pic}(G)$ choose $\chi$ with $\delta(\chi)=a$; then $na=\delta(n\chi)=0$ by step 2, since $\delta$ is a group homomorphism.

source.place: Proposition 18.22 and Corollary 18.23, printed pp.392–393; Proposition 18.18, sequence (129), printed p.391.

proof.text: Let $K/k$ be any field extension. By [lem-sfb-affine-group-picard-field-invariance], $p_K^*:\operatorname{Pic}(G)\to\operatorname{Pic}(G_K)$ is an isomorphism of abelian groups. For an invertible module $N$ on $G_K$, choose $a\in\operatorname{Pic}(G)$ with $p_K^*(a)=[N]$. Step 3 gives $n[N]=p_K^*(na)=p_K^*(0)=0$, which by the stated Picard group law means $N^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal O_{G_K}$. The integer $n$ chosen from $M$ in step 2 is independent of $K$ and $N$. No step assumes that $K$ is algebraic, separable or perfect. The argument also applies to the trivial group.

source.place: Lemma 2.3, pp.117–118, Remark 2.2(v), p.117, and Proposition 2.5 and the following paragraph, pp.118–119; primary publisher PDF read online, WANTED locally.

proof_origin.place: Corollary 18.23, p.393, using Propositions 18.18 and 18.22, pp.391–393; combined with Brion, On Linearization of Line Bundles, Lemma 2.3 and Proposition 2.5, pp.117–119 (WANTED locally, publisher PDF read online). The explicit finite-group and Hopf-algebra annihilator calculation is written by Q24.
